items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: In the band is about . . . what? There’s ten men on the stage. No, eight men on the stage, and the rest of them is all late. ... When I look around, Shad Collins, here he come. He sneak on.

ctx.x: There’s a new magazine that’s come out. He and I are real friends. His wife Lorraine was there. She was a chorus girl. Cab used to change chorus girls. A chorus girl would leave. There’s Lorraine traveling with Dizzy. She was a number one Apollo chorus, but he never would hire her. He could give her a job, since she’s with her husband. Wouldn’t that look plausible? But he didn’t. You’re looking all that. Chu Berry, him and Roy Eldridge want to go around every night. Every town they get in, they go look for…
So Dizzy was playing what became bebop.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And Shad Collins and all of us signed at the register and got rooms and went in there.

ctx.x: He wasn't a hunchback, was he? There was a guy named Mitch who had a hunchback.
You almost said it. Not (?), but a little cat. Looked something like Shad Collins. He had a name around Chicago.
It wasn't Tick Gray? Tick Gray.
